title: guard_frozen _resolve_vars reads quoted and shell-scoped assignments as the shell does
why: Lane agent-worktree-add-in-tool-dir (session_013NEJL382EZLqWkzVvjj7UP), 17:41 CST Nov 8, found in review of the follow-up to #1977 (variable worktree-add target). (1) `BASE=.claude/worktrees; WT="$BASE"/../lane` splits the value at the quote, so a write or worktree add lands somewhere other than the guard thinks (hooks/guard_frozen.py _resolve_vars about line 299; shared with _shell_write_hit about line 629). (2) A lone apostrophe in an earlier `echo "don't"` makes the `'[^']*'` match span segments, so a later reassignment is missed (about line 297). (3) A prefix assignment `S=x cmd "$S"` and a subshell `(S=x)` are read as setting S for later text, which the shell does not do. Each is a form Claude writes in normal work. The resolver feeds more than one rule, so it needs its own lane and review; the worktree-add follow-up reuses it as is. Rule building-scanner-respects-strings. Red cases: one per form above.
